notable_claims: State university policies banning 'trivial' or 'annoying' messages may be unconstitutionally vague.
Prohibiting anonymous userids on campus networks may violate established Supreme Court precedents on anonymous speech.
Granting a Director of Computer Services summary punishment authority over faculty and students may bypass required due process.
classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie provides a detailed critique of the University of Missouri-Rolla's computing policies, arguing that they are unconstitutionally vague and overbroad. He specifically challenges bans on anonymous posting, 'trivial' messages, and content others might find offensive, asserting these violate First Amendment rights and academic freedom. The post includes extensive references to case law and EFF resources regarding censorship and harassment in university settings.
classification.title: Re: Policies of the U. of Missouri-Rolla, Computer Services

identity.subject: Re: Policies of the U. of Missouri-Rolla, Computer Services
